raw_plan.expected_behavior: Valid inputs (formatted length <= 15) produce identical output via puts as the original; oversized inputs are rejected or truncated so the 16-byte buffer and canary are never overflowed, and the function returns normally after the canary check.

raw_plan.root_cause: The function formats an attacker-controlled input string into a fixed 16-byte stack buffer at [rbp-0x20] via sprintf with format at 0x10004cf, without bounding the output length, so inputs producing more than 15 bytes plus NUL overflow the buffer and adjacent stack (including the canary at [rbp-8]).
raw_plan.original_behavior: Stores the input pointer, calls sprintf(dest=[rbp-0x20], fmt=0x10004cf, input) with no length limit, then calls puts(dest), then verifies the stack canary and returns.
raw_plan.required_invariant: At most 15 bytes plus a NUL terminator are written into the 16-byte destination buffer; the stack canary at [rbp-8] and all memory outside [rbp-0x20, rbp-0x10) remain unmodified.
raw_plan.repair_strategy: Bound the formatted output to the 16-byte destination capacity before/while copying: reject or truncate inputs whose formatted length would exceed 15 bytes, ensuring the write to [rbp-0x20] never exceeds capacity-1 bytes plus NUL, while preserving the sprintf+puts sequence for valid inputs.
raw_plan.failure_behavior: For inputs that do not fit in 15 bytes, do not overflow the buffer; either skip the copy/print or emit a bounded/truncated result, then proceed to canary check and return without corrupting the stack.
raw_plan.expected_behavior: Valid inputs (formatted length <= 15) produce identical output via puts as the original; oversized inputs are rejected or truncated so the 16-byte buffer and canary are never overflowed, and the function returns normally after the canary check.
verification_conditions: Formatted output length is always <= 15 bytes plus NUL written to [rbp-0x20]
Stack canary at [rbp-8] is unchanged and canary check passes
puts is called with a NUL-terminated string within the 16-byte buffer for valid inputs

note: baseline is deterministic; AI target assembly is accepted only by native/qemu PoC+regression. baseline_target_strict calls repair_any(target=<case target>, require_target=True) and records the resolved target_scope plus target_in_scope (every produced action inside the target; empty action lists are not in scope). baseline_target_aware receives the same target/capacity hint; ai_blind uses the public AI path without target. allow_calls only permits direct calls already present in the target function.
evaluation_note: deterministic baselines run on the host; PoC evaluation and the unstripped x86-64 target execution run in the Linux guest (Lima) via the poc/guest runner. Provider prompts/responses are never stored.
